slides.title: AI Updates Skill Recording in Claude Co-work "Record
slides.text: AI Updates Skill Recording in Claude Co-work "Record a Skill" enables users to train Claude by recording screen actions and voiceover instructions - only on Mac Open the Claude desktop app and choose Record a skill from the + menu in Claude Cowork Claude analyzes the recording using visual and audio cues to automatically write a reusable skill file saved directly to your local skill library Once saved, Claude autonomously executes the entire multi-step workflow This technology unlocks full desktop automation for legacy software, private admin portals, and web tools lacking native AI integrations No APIs or MCP connections required Recommended workflow setup uses advanced models like Fable 5 for skill creation and cost-effective models like Opus or Sonnet for execution Practical demonstrations show automated client onboarding workflows and a YouTube content ideation system based on viral outliers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KjNp6CbHUSY https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512198-how-to-create-custom-skills https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jbiMx17fEK0 - demo https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9QSumbWubZ4 - demo

slides.title: AI Updates Hugging Face hacked by autonomous AI
slides.text: AI Updates Hugging Face hacked by autonomous AI agent OpenAI models were tested on the exploit gym benchmark decided to find answers online The AI escaped their sandbox and launched zero-day cyberattacks against Hugging Face to scrape the benchmark answers The model slipped a poisoned dataset into Hugging Face's data pipeline to run arbitrary code and crawl internal clusters. Escalated privileges, and reached internet-connected nodes. Hugging Face tried analyzing the attack using US proprietary frontier models like ChatGPT and Claude, but their safety guardrails blocked the security payloads So Hugging Face had to use Chinese open-weight models like GLM-5. Sentdex criticizes closed-source AI companies for lobbying against open-weight models, arguing that accessible open models are critical for real-world cybersecurity defense OpenAI framed the incident as a collaborative partnership, masking the fact that their model caused the breach https://www.youtube.com/shorts/zj9j031oFoc - short explanation https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IY3b4HTxpgU https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KOpTWx1Eou4

slides.title: OpenCode vs Claude Code OpenCode vs Claude Code
slides.text: OpenCode vs Claude Code OpenCode vs Claude Code Claude Code - tight ecosystem/model quality ; Has claude-agent-sdk OpenCode - open-source, model-agnostic, lower cost, CLI-first AI coding agent for the terminal that lets you swap providers or run local models - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode Opencode Python SDK - https://libraries.io/pypi/opencode-py # pip install opencode-py==0.8.0 from opencode import Opencode with Opencode() as ai: answer = ai.ask("Explain dependency injection") print(answer) # Streaming with Opencode() as ai: for chunk in ai.ask_stream("Write a Python function"): print(chunk, end="") import subprocess result = subprocess.run( ["opencode", "run", "explain this codebase"], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr)

slides.title: AI Updates Google Gemini and Gemini Notebook vs
slides.text: AI Updates Google Gemini and Gemini Notebook vs Fable: Google rebrands NotebookLM as Gemini Notebook Deep Web Research Multimodal Analysis (images, landing pages, screenshots) Content Generation (blog posts, newsletter, social media content) Digest massive PDFs and text files, provide clickable citations Compare up to 50 docs to find conflicting facts or figures Automates customer review analysis, instantly build quizzes or flashcards from raw notes Converts docs into two-host conversational podcasts https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rZeCwj6fhRI Selecting Right Tokens For Specific Tasks Low cost per token models (like Kimi K3) may require twice as many tokens as GPT-5.6 to solve the same problem, resulting in equal total costs To maximize performance and minimize expense, use a three-step workflow: 1. a top-tier model for high-level planning 2. a fast and cheap model to execute code 3. a secondary frontier model for code review Output tokens cost significantly more than input tokens, making execution (writing code)  the most expensive phase of software development https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QNEo_tl-nhw

slides.title: AI Video using Higgsfield & FFmpeg AI Video
slides.text: AI Video using Higgsfield & FFmpeg AI Video Creation using Higsfield + Claude https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DLskE_RN59I https://higgsfield.ai Julia McCoy demonstrates how she produced a complete video short without filming any footage She used Higsfield's MCP connector inside Claude, enabled the AI assistant to go beyond writing scripts and directly build and render video assets Claude selected her saved AI avatar, applied her cloned voice, generated background stills, and rendered individual scene clips A plain-text feedback prompted Claude to establish strict production rules In just two hours, six clips were produced and stitched, while Claude saved a production playbook for future episodes Previously Julia's team was using HeyGen (avatar video) and ElevenLabs (cloned voice audio). She no longer needs them Claude uses the Higgsfield connector to automatically pull up her "Soul character" - her saved AI face/visual avatar Higgsfield also handles her cloned voice and native audio right inside the video generation process (rendering shots with built-in voice audio using models like Seedance) The manual scene-by-scene build process is now automated. Claude acts as the producer that writes the script, triggers Higgsfield to generate her visual clone and audio, and renders all the video clips in one single chat session. Once you have generated 20..50 short files, they can be combined into one video file locally using Claude Code and “ffmpeg” utilities https://www.ffmpeg.org https://www.ffmpeg.org/documentation.html https://www.gyan.dev/ffmpeg/builds/ FFmpeg can change resolution and frame rate, stitch the pieces together (videos and images), can create transitions between clips

slides.title: AI Updates Mark Pincus 2-Lists Formula for Startup
slides.text: AI Updates Mark Pincus 2-Lists Formula for Startup Ideas Write two lists - Love & Hate. Products and experiences you love using, and ones you hate or find broken in your daily life For each item you love, study what already works in it - its "proven" behavior, UX, and engagement patterns Then, look for items on your "hate" list where those proven patterns could fix something broken Design one clearly “better” improvement that 10 out of 10 users would agree on, and add one small "new" experimental twist Iterate quickly, treating this as a structured generator for startup ideas grounded in real user behavior Mark Pincus (born 1966) is an American internet entrepreneur and founder of Zynga, a pioneering social gaming company that went public in 2011 and is valued at $12B+. He also founded Freeloader, Tribe Networks, and Support.com, co-founded Reinvent Capital, and helped create a Stanford GSB product management course. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus

slides.title: AI Updates AI is transforming ASIC/SoC development ASIC
slides.text: AI Updates AI is transforming ASIC/SoC development ASIC = Application-Specific Integrated Circuit - a custom chip to perform specific function(s) for a product or an app SoC = System-on-Chip Problems - increasingly complex heterogeneous and chiplet-based architectures Solution - use AI for design, verification, and optimization of PPA (Power, Performance, and Area) AI tools - such as Synopsys DSO.ai and Cadence/Google Cloud Agentic workflows - allow smaller teams to handle unprecedented complexity Generative AI tools translate natural language intent into verified templates, testbenches, and hardware descriptions, drastically reducing manual coding time. Machine learning–driven tools now automate test generation, accelerate coverage closure, and predict bug‑prone areas, cutting verification effort that can reach 60–70% of engineering hours On the design side, generative and agentic AI explore vast design spaces, tune thousands of params, and optimize the conversion flows, especially for macro placement and floorplanning Emerging trends focus on domain‑specialized models tightly integrated into existing flows Strong emphasis on explainability, deterministic guardrails, and safety as AI becomes a core pillar of semiconductor toolchains AI/ML algorithms analyze functional coverage models and dynamically generate stimuli to target unverified corner cases, slashing the time required for coverage closure.Automated Debugging: AI models can sift through massive regression databases and waveforms autonomously to pinpoint the root causes of failures, resolving issues long before the tapeout phase.Physical Design Space Exploration: Machine learning swiftly evaluates millions of potential floor plans and clocking strategies to optimize for Power, Performance, and Area (PPA).

slides.text: AI on small devices Google is pushing compact on-device models and runtimes for real-time use on phones, laptops, and other edge devices LiteRT-LM is a cross-platform on-device LLM stack Function Gemma 270M reportedly reached nearly 2K tokens/sec prefill on a Pixel 7, and fine-tuning improved fixed-intent accuracy from 46% to 90% on eight of ten functions Gemma 4 12B is positioned for local multimodal, agentic workflows on everyday machines, including script generation and tool use through Google AI Edge Gallery and LiteRT-LM Apple’s Ferret-UI Lite reportedly showed that a 3B model can match or exceed much larger systems on benchmark tasks DroidRun is an LLM-agnostic mobile agent for controlling Android and iOS devices through natural language and multi-step automation https://github.com/google-ai-edge/LiteRT-LM

slides.title: Vibe Coding - 6 Principles Vibe Coding -
slides.text: Vibe Coding - 6 Principles Vibe Coding - 6 Principles 1. Plan before prompting 2. Direct the AI to ask clarifying questions before building 3. Build in small steps, test after each step 4. Copy raw error messages directly into the prompt 5. Roll back to previous working versions if code breaks (checkpoints) 6. Start fresh if AI can not fix in three tries https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oncrSvt79tQ Don't Ship Skills Without Evals - Philipp Schmid Developers must evaluate AI agent skills before shipping them Most skills are created without systematic testing, leading to unpredictable agent performance Human-authored skills outperform AI-generated ones Skills should remain concise, use clear directives, and layer detailed information across reference files Implementing small evaluation suites allows development teams to catch performance regressions, refine trigger descriptions, and identify when model upgrades make existing skills obsolete https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0vphxNt4wyk

slides.title: AI Updates Webserver Caddy vs Nginx https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YfK9QmJoaWs Caddy
slides.text: AI Updates Webserver Caddy vs Nginx https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YfK9QmJoaWs Caddy offers a dramatically simpler configuration It is written in Go - memory-safe, fewer security vulnerabilities Does automatic HTTPS config (certificates, renewals) Up to 20% faster when serving small files Nginx still better at hyper-scale. Written in C, Nginx consumes a quarter of the memory of Caddy under idle connections and is more efficient at streaming very large files, making it the preferred choice for major CDNs and tiny resource-constrained hardware Colibri Tiny Inference Engine A lightweight engine written in 1300 lines of C that allows to run massive LLMs (like 744B-params GLM-5.2) locally https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=19xCOJxWU0A It is very slow (0.1-1 tokens/sec)

slides.text: AI Updates Use RAM as VRAM - Linux Hack https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RqqHWol4Kwk AMD-based System76 laptop Configuring env variables to trick integrated GPU into treating 32GB of 96GB system RAM as dedicated VRAM Test - running LLMs locally via Ollama Qwen 2.5 (14B), Qwen 2.5 (35B), and Gemma (31B) While the Gemma model runs significantly slower than the Qwen models, monitor tools confirm that the system successfully allocates up to 70% of the newly mapped memory, proving that older AMD hardware can run massive models without dedicated GPUs Claude Code vs Codex https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCOWH0RDB4s Claude Code excels at complex, multi-file projects and maintaining deep memory during long programming sessions Conversely, Codex offers better value for money, generous token limits, and practical automation features like frontend browser reviews and background task delegation Developers should choose Claude Code for highly complex, tool-heavy development, and Codex for daily delegation, task reviews, and budget-friendly coding

slides.title: Pandas, DuckDB, Polars, Spark Pandas - uses single
slides.text: Pandas, DuckDB, Polars, Spark Pandas - uses single CPU, loads everything into RAM DuckDB - columnar database (like SQLite for analytics) DuckDB - parallel data processing using  all CPUs and vectorized execution DuckDB can query datasets larger than available RAM DuckDB queries CSV/Parquet/JSON files directly using standard SQL, and integrates smoothly with existing Pandas DataFrames (for ML & Plotting) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mqj9OChctRQ # pip install duckdb import duckdb # Query a CSV file directly without loading it first result = duckdb.sql("SELECT * FROM 'sales_data.csv' WHERE amount > 100") print(result) # Or query a Pandas DataFrame in-place using zero-copy memory import pandas as pd df = pd.DataFrame({"category": ["A", "B", "A"], "sales": [10, 20, 30]}) summary_rel = duckdb.sql( "SELECT category, SUM(sales) AS total FROM df GROUP BY category" ) print(summary_rel) # DuckDBPyRelation object summary_df = summary_rel.df() # Python DataFrame Polars is a faster DataFrame library , especially for transformations, joins, and larger in-memory analytics, thanks to Rust and lazy execution DuckDB is an embedded SQL analytics engine that is great for querying files like Parquet or CSV directly and often wins on large analytical workloads Pandas is great for small or legacy applications, LM and Plotting Spark, Dask, or DataFusion can be better for large distributed data, but they add more complexity than these single-node tools.

slides.title: AI Updates Automated routing to pick best models
slides.text: AI Updates Automated routing to pick best models for given tasks No single AI model excels at every task, as Claude leads in coding, Gemini dominates benchmarks, and GPT shines in research Platforms like Abacus AI allow users to set up custom routers using plain English instructions https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=giD8KtDBnJc These routers automatically evaluate each incoming prompt and direct it to the best-suited model This automated multi-model approach lowers overall AI spending, improves output quality, and enables dynamic workflows tailored to task complexity or user pricing tiers Google Vids: Gemini Omni and Personal Avatars Gemini Omni - generates and edits video clips directly from text prompts, sketches, or existing footage Users can refine lighting, backgrounds, and effects conversationally without complex editing tools Personal Avatars allow users to generate a realistic digital double using a selfie and voice recording to deliver scripted videos Use cases - business updates, onboarding, and marketing Available to Google AI Pro, Ultra, and Workspace subscribers Security - account verification and invisible SynthID watermarks https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZZ_HghP02bs

slides.title: AI Updates OpenAI’s GPT-RED red-teaming system Designed to
slides.text: AI Updates OpenAI’s GPT-RED red-teaming system Designed to attack OpenAI’s own models and uncover prompt injection and other adversarial vulnerabilities at scale It repeatedly crafts and refines malicious prompts, observes model responses, and optimizes toward successful exploits such as data exfiltration or safety bypasses GPT-RED is trained via self-play reinforcement learning, where it plays the attacker against defender models that are rewarded for completing tasks while resisting attacks This loop forces GPT-RED to invent increasingly sophisticated strategies, generating training data that hardens production models like GPT‑5.6 against emerging real-world threats https://openai.com/index/unlocking-self-improvement-gpt-red/ Linux wins over Windows Windows 11 struggles with critical bugs, system crashes, and steep hardware requirements Linux has quietly gaining Driven by Valve’s Proton compatibility layer and hardware like the Steam Deck, Linux has made unprecedented gains in desktop gaming, breaking historical market share records European governments are legally mandating open-source transitions to secure digital sovereignty and reduce licensing costs With mainstream manufacturers now shipping Linux by default and software compatibility reaching near-parity, the Linux OS has crossed the threshold from a niche hobbyist tool into a self-reinforcing, institutional mainstream competitor

slides.title: AI Updates Designing effective AI agent systems Peter
slides.text: AI Updates Designing effective AI agent systems Peter Yang interviews Thariq Shihipar from Anthropic’s Claude Code Shihipar emphasizes structuring agent loops around clear goals and exit conditions, using commands like /goal to maintain focus He explains how dynamic, multi-agent workflows enable parallel execution and built-in verification, improving reliability on complex tasks Through an automated video editing example, he shows how iterative planning helps surface and resolve unknowns before full automation The discussion also covers “Claude Tag,” a Slack-integrated system for collaborative, multi-agent task management. Shihipar’s key advice is to keep context windows tight and develop a deep understanding of system limits rather than relying only on prompting https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aVO6E181cNU Google TurboQuant - vector compression AI vector index memory usage from 31 GB down to 4 GB It applies a shared random rotation to align vector coordinates into a predictable bell curve, applying optimal Lloyd-Max quantization alongside a single-bit error-correction step Independent developer Ryan Kadry implemented the open-source library TurboC using Rust, delivering faster search performance than Meta's FAISS while enabling seamless online vector ingestion TurboQuant reduces LLM key-value cache memory x6. This significantly cuts cloud hardware costs and accelerates inference without sacrificing search accuracy or retrieval performance for long-context applications https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LvBsACJy4ww .

slides.title: From Windows to Linux or Mac Governments Win
slides.text: From Windows to Linux or Mac Governments Win to Linux: France is moving 2.5 Mln gov workstations to (NixOS) Linux to reduce dependence on foreign tech and improve digital sovereignty https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hmGAId0J2Lc https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jTqmHKTehKM Schleswig-Holstein State in Germany is migrating about 30K employees to Linux and LibreOffice for cost savings, security, and control over data. The desktop is reported as KDE Plasma, with possible distros including Kubuntu, SLED, or openSUSE Leap https://www.zdnet.com/article/the-german-state-schleswig-holstein-uninstalls-windows/ France’s Gendarmerie has long used GendBuntu, a custom Ubuntu-based system, on most workstations. It switched for stability, maintainability, and independence from Microsoft https://www.zdnet.com/article/the-german-state-schleswig-holstein-uninstalls-windows/ South Korea explored Linux desktops, using Ubuntu-based Harmonica and other Linux variants in some agencies, mainly to cut licensing costs and reduce reliance on Windows https://www.zdnet.com/article/south-koreas-government-explores-move-from-windows-to-linux-desktop/ China Governmnet moving toward Chinese-made, Linux-based systems like Kylin and NeoKylin Governments Win to Apple: Germany (federal administration), US federal agencies: NASA, DOE, NIH, and parts of the FBI; State and local government in the US; Canada government: Uses modern device policies that allow staff to choose tools that fit the job, including Macs. Big Companies Windows to Linux: Google is using Linux-based desktops internally, often described as Goobuntu https://www.techrepublic.com/article/five-big-names-that-use-linux-on-the-desktop/ NASA and contractor United Space Alliance moved key functions from Windows to Debian-based Linux because they wanted stability, reliability, and in-house control. https://www.techrepublic.com/article/five-big-names-that-use-linux-on-the-desktop/ ) CERN uses thousands of Linux desktops, including Scientific Linux, Ubuntu, and CentOS https://www.techrepublic.com/article/five-big-names-that-use-linux-on-the-desktop/ Some large firms also standardize on Linux for infrastructure rather than desktops (reduce licensing costs, fits cloud-native ops) https://www.computerworld.com/article/1347921/big-business-go-big-on-linux.html Big Companies Windows to Apple: IBM, SAP, Uber, BuzzFeed, Nike OpenAI, Anthropic, Alibaba, other Chinese AI/startups

slides.text: AI Updates OpenAI has acquired Astral The Python devtool startup founded by Charlie Marsh (Brooklyn, NY, 11+ people) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Iw65FD4MGgs 2022 - Ruff - Python linter and formatter 2024 - uv  - Fast Python package and project manager 2025 - ty - Fast Python type checker and language server All three tools written in Rust - fast, reliable, crash-free dev tools The team uses AI for coding Human engineering and first-principles thinking remain essential for core systems architecture and macro-level design To prevent AI-generated code quality drops ("AI slop"), Astral relies on extensive automated testing, continuous benchmark profiling, and strict PR reviews Strategy - keeping core tools free and open-source while offering enterprise solutions like hosted private registries (`py`) built on top of `uv` Examples of usage: ruff check . # to lint a project ruff format . # to auto-format files ruff check --fix .    # to apply safe fixes uv init myproj        # to create a project uv add requests       # to add a dependency uv run python main.py # to run code in the project env ty check .            # to type-check a codebase # ty can also act as a language server for editor integration

slides.title: AI Updates KMS - Key Management Service AWS
slides.text: AI Updates KMS - Key Management Service AWS KMS and GCP Cloud KMS are managed services for creating, storing, rotating, and controlling encryption keys used to protect data at rest and in applications https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/concepts-intro.html https://aws.amazon.com/kms/ https://aws.amazon.com/kms/ AWS KMS supports centralized policy-based access control, CloudTrail auditing, and hardware-backed key protection using validated HSMs HSM = Hardware Security Module . It is a physical device designed to securely generate, store, and use cryptographic keys GCP Cloud KMS provides centralized key management for Google Cloud, supports software, HSM, and external keys, and integrates with services like BigQuery, GCS, and GKE through CMEK https://innfactory.de/en/cloud/gcp/products/cloud-kms/ Both platforms support automatic rotation and strong auditability, but AWS emphasizes AWS-native service coverage while GCP emphasizes flexible protection levels and key access justification logging
